text: Merey 16 (27 Mbbl) secures 22 days cover for Jamnagar (1240 kbd), extending baseline from 15 to 37 days. Heavy slate (55% resid, 262 ppm Ni+V) maximizes RIL's coker yield but demands $4.2/bbl desulfurization premium. Binding constraint: OFAC GL 50A compliance; payment via AMBER rail requires per-cargo comfort letter by Day 40. Cargo arrives Day 55, creating a 10-day supply gap requiring strategic drawdown. Cost is elevated freight ($18/bbl) due to long-haul reroute. This option buys critical runtime continuity against Hormuz closure but locks capital in high-risk Venezuelan paper until sanctions clarity confirms at Day 45. Reversibility is zero post-loading; traceability mandates full chain-of-custody audit under Article A7.

MEMO — Merey 16 to Jamnagar. Approve CONDITIONAL: 1) Secure GL 50A comfort letter pre-loading; 2) Cap exposure at 15% of 15-day baseline (277 kb); 3) Confirm A7 traceability via independent inspector. Heavy sour (16° API, 2.45% S) fits Jamnagar complex yield; Ni+V 262 ppm within catalyst tolerance. Payment via AMBER rail only. Freight premium estimated $1.80/bbl vs. Basrah given voyage length and insurance.

Girassol (API 30.2, S 0.343%) secures 16 Mb for Jamnagar (1,240 kbd), extending cover from 15 to 26 days. Arrival Day 35 bridges the Hormuz gap. Cost: Premium freight + USD LC liquidity strain. Binding constraint: 49.4% resid yield demands coker throughput; TAN 0.39 limits blending ratios. Timing reality: Cargo availability lags immediate burn rate by five weeks, creating a critical inventory drawdown window. This option buys volume certainty against Angola's stable export rail but locks capital in a single-origin basket, testing Concentration Cap (A3). Reversibility is low post-loading; traceability remains high under USD settlement. Execute only if coker margins sustain heavy sour processing.

MEMO — Girassol to Jamnagar. Approve CONDITIONAL:
1. Verify A4 sanctions clearance on Angolan sup chain within 48h.
2. Confirm A6 reversibility clause for cargo diversion if TAN >0.45 upon loading.
3. Secure A2 security floor insurance for Gulf of Guinea transit leg.

High-resid (49.43%) fits Jamnagar coker capacity; low sulfur (0.343%) maximizes DTA margin. 16k bbl covers 1.3 days baseline; deploy against 15-day cover target. USD LC greenlit.

Sizing: 16,000 kb @ $3.20/bbl freight premium vs. WTI; total landed cost $74.50/bbl.

**Proposal:** Divert 45 Mb WTI Midland (API 44.5, S 0.32%) USGC→Jamnagar. ETA Day 38.
**Value:** Adds +36 days cover (total 51d); maximizes high-yield diesel/jet from DTA/SEZ units. Light sweet feed offsets heavy sour deficit.
**Cost:** Premium freight +$4.2/bbl; USD LC liquidity strain.
**Constraint:** A3 Concentration Cap. Single-cargo reliance breaches diversification thresholds unless paired with African slate.
**Timing:** Critical gap Days 20–38. Cargo availability aligns with inventory drawdown cliff.
**Risk:** A5 Uncertainty—Hormuz closure persists; reroute viability hinges on USGC loading window stability.
**Action:** Execute spot fix subject to A4 Sanctions clearance. Immediate LC issuance required to secure berth priority. This buys time, not a solution.

MEMO — WTI Midland to Jamnagar. Approve CONDITIONAL: 1) Verify A4 sanctions clearance on USGC supplier within 24h; 2) Confirm A6 reversal clause for cargo diversion if Jamnagar intake exceeds 90% capacity by Day 25. WTI specs (44.5° API, 0.32% S) align perfectly with RIL complex yield optimization. 45,000 kb covers 3.6 days of 1,240 kbd throughput, lifting inventory from 15 to 18.6 days. USD LC rail active. Freight delta vs. Brent benchmark estimated at -$1.80/bbl netback gain. Execution window tight: load Day 20, arrive Jamnagar Day 35.

Urals (API 31.8, S 1.35%) fits Jamnagar's complex yield slate perfectly; 30 Mb covers 24 days, extending runway to Day 39. Cost: capped at $44.10/bbl via AMBER rail, saving ~$12/bbl vs. Middle East sour alternatives. Binding constraint: EU/G7 price-cap attestation required before loading; failure triggers total embargo. Timing reality: Cargo available Day 64, but India's 15-day baseline expires Day 15. This gap is fatal without interim bridging. Option survives only if we secure short-term charters to hold cargo offshore or accelerate discharge logistics. Without immediate waiver validation, this volume is stranded inventory, not supply relief. Action: Validate attestation chain within 48 hours or reject.

MEMO — Urals-to-Jamnagar Waiver. Approve CONDITIONAL:
1. Supplier attests price ≤$44.10/bbl per EU 18th Package; docs uploaded to AMBER rail pre-loading.
2. Cargo capped at 15% of Jamnagar baseline cover (4.5M bbl) to satisfy A3 Concentration.
3. Full Ni+V (71 ppm) and resid (47%) yield modeling confirmed for DTA tax optimization.
4. Reversibility clause active if G7 cap drops below $40.00 before day 64.
Net landed cost est. $46.80/bbl; 30M bbl volume secures 24-day extension to baseline cover.

Draw 18.6 MMbbl from Jamnagar SPR (15-day baseline) to sustain 1,240 kbd throughput for 15 days. Cost: $1.4B at $75/bbl replacement; opportunity loss of $900M vs. spot arbitrage. Binding constraint: A3 Concentration Cap limits single-site draw to 40% of total national reserve, capping extension at 6 days without violating security floors. Timing: Logistics lag requires T+24h authorization to hit pumps by T+48h; full depletion occurs Day 16. This option buys immediate grid stability and prevents DTA/SEZ shutdown but exhausts local buffers before alternative sea-lanes open. Irreversible once pipeline pressure drops below 80%. Traceability logs confirm sovereign custody under A7.

MEMO — Strategic Reserve Draw. Approve CONDITIONAL: 1) Cap release at 220 kbd to respect A3 concentration limits; 2) Mandate real-time A7 traceability tags on all barrels entering SEZ; 3) Enforce A6 reversibility clause triggering automatic refill if Brent dips below $75. Draw 18.6 Mb total (15-day baseline gap) over 21 days. Estimated logistics premium: $0.45/bbl.

Execute 300 kb/d demand cut paired with product-import swap for 30 days. Net relief: 180 kb/d diesel equivalent. Cost: $420M premium + 0.4% GDP drag. Binding constraint: Gulf Coast/Europe surplus capacity caps swap volume at 250 kb/d; remainder requires domestic refinery run-slashing. Timing: T+72 hours for tender, T+14 days for first cargo arrival. This option buys immediate inventory stabilization without breaching A3 concentration caps or A4 sanctions lines. Reversibility (A6) is high post-crisis; traceability (A7) remains intact via digital bills of lading. Uncertainty (A5): Freight rates may spike 40%. Security floor (A2) holds as strategic reserves remain untouched. Completeness (A1) achieved by covering 60% of the supply gap immediately.

MEMO — Demand-side run-cut / product-import swap, 300 kb/d for 30 days. Approve CONDITIONAL: 1) Verify A4 sanctions clearance on source cargo within 4 hours; 2) Cap counterparty exposure at 15% per A3; 3) Embed A6 auto-reversion trigger if inventory dips below security floor. Net supply impact: +9.0 MMbbl over tenure. Estimated swap premium: $0.45/bbl ($4.05 MM total).

Divert 2.1 Mbbl owned on-water cargo to Kochi (BPCL). Extends baseline cover from 11 to 18 days immediately. Cost: $4.2M diversion fees + $0.85/bbl demurrage. Binding constraint: Kochi's single-point mooring limits intake to 180 kbd; full discharge requires 12 days, creating a temporary throughput bottleneck against the 310 kbd refining capacity. Timing is critical: arrival T+4 days prevents stockout at T+11. This tranche secures A2 (Security floor) for Southern India without triggering A3 (Concentration cap) breaches elsewhere. Reversibility (A6) remains intact until final berthing. Action locks in 7 days of critical runway while diplomatic channels address the Hormuz closure.

MEMO — Owned on-water cargo diverted to Kochi (tranche 1). Approve CONDITIONAL: 1) Verify A4 Sanctions transparency via immediate bill-of-lading audit; 2) Enforce A3 Concentration cap limiting Kochi intake to 45 kbd over 72 hours to prevent baseline cover breach >14 days; 3) Confirm A6 Reversibility protocol with alternate berth at Mumbai within 12 hours. Diversion adds $0.85/bbl freight; net uplift $2.10/bbl vs. spot.

Divert 2.1 Mbbl owned on-water cargo to Kochi (BPCL). Extends baseline cover from 11 to 18 days, buying critical runway for diplomatic de-escalation. Cost: $4.2M premium plus $180k/day demurrage risk. Binding constraint: A3 Concentration Cap; Kochi intake cannot exceed 85% of nameplate without violating safety protocols, limiting discharge to 263 kbd. Timing reality: ETA 96 hours; full integration into tanks requires T+7 days due to single-point mooring bottlenecks. This tranche prevents immediate rationing but exhausts A6 Reversibility; once diverted, cargo cannot re-route if Strait opens within 48 hours. Execute only if closure probability exceeds 80% at T+24h.

MEMO — Owned on-water cargo diverted to Kochi (tranche 2). Approve CONDITIONAL: 1) Verify A4 sanctions clearance within 4h of berth assignment; 2) Cap BPCL intake at 280 kbd to maintain A3 concentration headroom below 90%; 3) Confirm A6 reversal window remains open until pipeline pressure stabilizes. Diversion adds $0.45/bbl freight vs. baseline; net cover extends to 14 days against 310 kbd throughput.

Hold 2.0Mb VLCC parcel offshore Mumbai. Cost: $12.50/bbl/day all-in (freight + demurrage). Buys 45-day supply buffer against total Hormuz closure, decoupling physical receipt from spot panic pricing. Binding constraint: A3 Concentration Cap limits exposure to 15% of national strategic reserve; further accumulation requires cabinet waiver. Timing reality: Discharge window closes T+21 days as port congestion hits critical mass; decision to land or re-export must be locked by T+14. A6 Reversibility allows immediate diversion to alternative buyers if sanctions landscape shifts under A4. This is not inventory; it is paid optionality on sovereign energy security.

MEMO — Floating Storage: 2,000 kb VLCC. Approve CONDITIONAL:
1. A2 Security Floor: Verify $4.50/bbl daily burn vs. forward curve contango; terminate if spread narrows < $0.80.
2. A3 Concentration Cap: Limit exposure to 15% of total book; hard stop at 300 kb net long.
3. A6 Reversibility: Secure confirmed discharge slots within 45 days; penalty clause triggered if delayed >72 hours.
4. A4 Sanctions: Full KYC on cargo origin and vessel history; zero tolerance for obscured beneficial ownership.

Cost: $9.0MM monthly opex + $0.12/bbl insurance premium; max hold 60 days.
